solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: E.g. calamari and cod help OAPs in need of treatment

definitions.note: calamari are squid rings, and squid belong to this class of sea creatures; plural, like the answer

indicators.note: something needing treatment is out of order, so the letters of the three words before are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Seafood dishes ordered for pensioners who need looking after.
explanation.walkthrough: Squid and octopus are the commonest members of the class; 'and' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid served as calamari is a typical member of the mollusc class with tentacles round the head.

clue.text: Priest comes round on Sunday to concentrate

indicators.note: the word comes goes round the priest's abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman doing his rounds on the Sabbath, perhaps to focus minds.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze something into a smaller space is to condense it, as a concentrate is made.

clue.text: Diplomat cleverly engages opponents in game number 15

definitions.note: refers to the 15-across solution, a famous fake

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so one piece sits inside the other
worked cleverly, the letters of the word Diplomat are rearranged

parts.note: in bridge West and North sit on opposing sides, so W and N are opponents

explanation.surface: A diplomat outwitting rivals in a game, finishing as number fifteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of DIPLOMAT take W and N inside; the final N is number. The 1912 skull was exposed as a forgery in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: The early-human skull 'found' in Sussex is the most famous scientific forgery, so it is an example of a fraud.

clue.text: Match takes place over in beer garden

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the letters are read upwards, back to front
in says the letters are found within the words beer garden

explanation.surface: A football match being shown in a pub beer garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EERGA sit inside 'beer garden'; read backwards they give the answer. 'takes place' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that match correspond, and to correspond is to concur or tally.

clue.text: Old Amazonians Cricket Club retire and head back

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the words before it are read backwards

parts.note: the Tupi are a people of the Amazon basin in Brazil

explanation.surface: Former players of an Amazonian cricket club retiring and heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tupi are an Amazonian people; 'retire' turns both the people and the club's initials round together.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical term names the rear part of the skull, the back of the head.

clue.text: There's another supply where you are

indicators.note: supply here is the adjective, pliant or flexible, so the word another bends into a new order

explanation.surface: A notice that more stock is available nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is the adjective (supple), signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone reading lives on this planet, so the phrase locates the reader in the world.

clue.text: Pick up tins (except in Kansas) in food outlets

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up raises the word, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tins are cans

indicators.note: in places one piece within the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: KS is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kansas
bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: Shopping advice: buy tinned goods at the food shops, unless in Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' works as a reversal only in a down clue; 'except' is bar, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafes selling light meals and quick bites are places that sell food.

clue.text: See 2
7A perhaps interrupts boss, as 15 did

definitions.note: the 15-across solution, a fraud, led people astray; past tense matches

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: MD, managing director, is a boss
the 7-across entry is an island in the Irish Sea, an example of an isle

explanation.surface: An islander breaks into the boss's meeting, as somebody did before.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7-across light names an island in the Irish Sea, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example; the definition points to the famous fraud at 15.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud deceives; the forgery fooled scientists for forty years, giving them wrong ideas.

clue.text: They make 6 get cosy

definitions.meaning: the Swiss food company that makes chocolate products sold in snack outlets, read as a name
to settle snugly against someone or into a comfortable place

explanation.surface: Confectioners making chocolate bars that are snug and comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: The company name is spelt with an accent on the final E, which the grid ignores.
explanation.definitionFit: The confectionery maker's name doubles as the verb for snuggling up comfortably.

clue.text: It helps to munch onion, leeks and radishes for starters

definitions.text: It helps to munch onion, leeks and radishes for starters

indicators.note: starters are beginnings, so each word's opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something useful for chewing your way through raw vegetables at the start of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the first letters of munch, onion, leeks, and, radishes spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding teeth at the back of the jaw do the chewing of tough raw vegetables.

clue.text: About end of 90s Versace's displayed plunging cleavages

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the last character of 90s is S

explanation.surface: Late-nineties Versace dresses with plunging necklines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' is a link. Cleavage also means a split, which is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep cracks in a glacier are splits that plunge downwards, so plunging cleavages describes them.

clue.text: Perhaps 'Morning Star' holds record for a fruit

indicators.note: holds says the newspaper keeps a new piece in its body
for says one piece stands in place of the named letter

parts.note: the Morning Star is a British communist daily, an example of a left-wing newspaper
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A left-wing daily keeps its record for a quantity of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Morning Star is Britain's communist newspaper, a red paper; EP replaces its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum is botanically a fruit, though usually eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Awesome ring given by king to his mistress

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A splendid ring given by a king to his lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awesome' looks like praise for a jewel but means solemn, awe-inspiring; the ring is a bell's.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow tolling of a bell for a death is a solemn, awe-inspiring sound.

clue.text: Carpenters' output was withdrawn and Springfield's cut

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word was is read backwards
cut means the end of the name is lopped off

parts.note: Dusty Springfield was a 1960s British singer

explanation.surface: Pop history: a Carpenters record withdrawn and Dusty Springfield's track cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carpenters were a US pop duo, but here they are woodworkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodworkers sawing timber produce fine wood particles as a by-product.

clue.text: Obsequious clerk in uniform locks up crate, say

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: locks of hair

indicators.note: say signals a word that is spoken and spelt differently

parts.note: crate and heap are both slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: A uniformed official locking up a packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: The fawning clerk is from Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's ever-'umble legal clerk is the byword for oily servility.

clue.text: Height of oak said to be deceptive

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, and spelt differently on paper

parts.note: 'of oak' becomes the possessive oak's

explanation.surface: A claim about the height of an oak tree that turns out misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of oak' is read as the possessive oak's, which sounds like OAX.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone with a trick is to act deceitfully, the verb sense needed after 'to'.

clue.text: Oyez! New 'Itunes' breaks record!

indicators.note: to break into something is to enter it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: new makes the word that follows into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A town crier announcing that iTunes has broken a sales record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal and 'breaks' the container; Oyez is the town crier's traditional call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier's call commands attention, like the modern order to pay attention.

clue.text: Article goes over province's struggle

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: over says one word covers the other, lying over it on each side

parts.note: taken as written
NI, Northern Ireland, is the Province, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a regional struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called the Province; its possessive gives NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to wrestle mentally, so a struggle over a decision fits.

clue.text: See 20
Mozart's pieces help tourist attraction in Med

parts.note: Mozart's works are catalogued by Köchel numbers, K nos for short
SOS is a call for help

explanation.surface: Mozart concertos played to help a Mediterranean tourist site.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's works are numbered in the Köchel catalogue, K numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minoan palace site on Crete draws visitors to the Mediterranean island.

clue.text: M&S stock one, only one, limited colour in so-called 2/7A

definitions.note: the Sussex skull hoax was claimed to be the gap between ape and human

indicators.note: to stock is to carry goods, so the store's initials hold a piece inside

parts.note: M&S is Marks and Spencer, the British chain store
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: single means only one
to ink a drawing is to colour it in

explanation.surface: Marks and Spencer stocking a single limited-edition colour.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British high-street chain; SINGLE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: The fake Sussex skull was hailed as the evolutionary intermediate between apes and humans.

clue.text: Spots almost seamless transformation

indicators.note: a transformation changes form, so the letters are reworked
almost means all but the final letter

explanation.surface: A fashion change that is nearly seamless.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAMLESS loses its final S to give SEAMLES, then 'transformation' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The childhood illness is known for a red rash of blotches over the skin.

clue.text: He serves wino regularly in Elstree area

parts.note: a stud is a male horse that serves, or covers, mares

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A waiter pouring wine at a film-world venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Elstree, north of London, is home to famous film and TV studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree is a centre of film-making, whose production spaces are sound stages and filming rooms.

clue.text: Plant remains in fine soil dug over with spades

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: soil that is dug over is turned and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Plant debris left in fine soil that has been turned with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant remains' reads as a gardener's debris but means preserved prehistoric traces.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric vegetation preserved in rock is one type of petrified remains.

clue.text: It erupts as warning to Herculaneum at first

parts.note: a toot of a horn is a warning

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter

explanation.surface: Vesuvius erupts, giving a warning to the Roman town of Herculaneum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupts' evokes Vesuvius burying Herculaneum, but a molar also erupts through the gum.
explanation.definitionFit: A new molar or incisor breaks through the gum, which dentists call erupting.

clue.text: Primate, old, called union before Brown

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: An old primate called on the union before a man named Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The Piltdown jaw was in fact from this ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-haired great ape of Borneo and Sumatra is a member of the primate order.

clue.text: He has a go at rock by Queen

definitions.note: a person who mocks; a noun phrase like the answer

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, Gib for short
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A climber attempting a rock face near the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a go at' suggests attempting, but here it means mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who jeers or taunts is attacking others with words.

clue.text: Ring round theatres backing school broadcast

indicators.note: round says the first piece goes all the way round the others

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them

indicators.note: backing means moving back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: reps are repertory theatres

explanation.surface: A call round theatres that back a school's broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns only the theatres round; 'broadcast' is the definition, as in scattering seed, not a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the noun means spreading out.

clue.text: Thiamine's for doctor

definitions.note: slang for a doctor, as in Star Trek's ship's surgeon

parts.note: thiamine is vitamin B1, giving the letter of the vitamin
the figure in the vitamin's name, written as a word, plus the possessive

explanation.surface: A vitamin as a doctor's prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: Thiamine is vitamin B1; read 'B one's' as a word. Sawbones is slang for a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a medical man, short for sawbones, used for Star Trek's ship's surgeon McCoy.

clue.text: Headless chicken's relative

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a chicken is a fowl

explanation.surface: A relative running around like a headless chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: one bird kin to another, and the chicken loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal bird of prey is a feathered relative of farmyard poultry.

clue.text: In supplements, comic strips cost about a penny

indicators.note: about places the words before it around the next piece
comic suggests something funny and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is a penny in British currency

explanation.surface: Newspaper supplements in which comic strips cost about a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges the two words, and 'about' wraps them round the penny; the supplements are additions to a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Additions written after a letter's signature are extra material appended to it.
